scene.name: Fan and floor friction
assumptions: The notes provide the calibrated box size (0.2 m per side), fan blade radius (0.15 m), hub height (0.6 m), box mass (0.1 kg), and approximate fan-to-box distance (1 m).
The shaft is aimed from the hub at the box center. The wake starts at the rotor origin.
The drawn floor is modeled as a finite 6 m by 2 m rigid platform, with its top face at Y=0. The fan stand has a 0.3 m foot and a narrow rigid post.
The fan rotor is approximated by a rigid hub and three rectangular blades; its 0.2 kg mass and 0.05 Nm finite motor effort are assumed.
The fan uses the zero motor target as the control, wake spread 0.25, wake range 2 m, and box drag coefficient 1.05 over 0.04 m² frontal area.
A fan tip ratio of 0.1 is assumed for the ideal actuator-disk model.
Contact friction values are assumed. Bodies are rigid; the fan wake is an idealized finite conical actuator-disk model, not resolved airflow.
This editable comparison uses manually corrected geometry from the recorded fan interpretation.
The floor and box contact coefficients are set to 0.001 for the low-friction comparison.

source.notes:
An electric fan on a fixed stand, switched on, blows air at a light box resting on the floor about 1 m in front of it. Fan blade radius about 15 cm, hub about 60 cm above the floor. The box is about 20 cm on each side and light (about 0.1 kg).

Comparison using a manually corrected interpretation of this drawing.
explanations: The long horizontal ground line is modeled as a finite floor platform.
The vertical support and short ground-level foot are represented as a fixed stand, with an inferred compact stator housing at the hub.
The central hub and three drawn radial strokes are represented as a single rotating hub-and-blade rigid body; the noted 0.15 m radius calibrates the blade tips.
The drawn box rests on the floor; its size, mass, and approximate distance from the fan use the provided notes.
